entries.message:
Google Ads integration is live on Adapty Attribution :rocket:

Adapty now pulls Google Ads performance data into UA analytics and sends conversion events back to Google for attribution and campaign optimization.

What customers can do now:

See Google Ads spend, impressions, clicks and conversions inside Adapty
Send installs, trial starts, purchases, renewals and other subscription events back to Google
Use Revenue Override to assign a value to trial events, so Google can optimize toward revenue and not just trial volume
Send test conversion events to check the setup before launching campaigns

Docs: <https://adapty.io/docs/ua-google-ads|adapty.io/docs/ua-google-ads>

entries.name: hey team!
entries.message:
hey team!
*You can now attach images in the Flow Agent chat* :frame_with_picture:
Until now you could only message the agent with text, so "make it like this" had to be explained in words. Now you can just show it.

*What you can do:*
• *Reference:* drop a screenshot and ask "make a similar screen." The agent builds the screen from builder elements in similar colors.
• *Your own image in the flow:* "set this as the background / hero / icon," and the image goes into an image element.
• *Screen feedback:* "this button looks off here, fix it," and the agent fixes the visuals.
Attach with the button or drag and drop into the chat. The agent remembers images in later messages of the thread, so you don't need to resend them.

*Not there yet, but coming soon:*
• *The agent doesn't generate images. If the reference has an illustration that isn't among the attachments, you'll get a placeholder or icons in its place.*
• One thread works with one screen, so three screenshots won't turn into three screens.
Give it a try and share your feedback :raised_hands:

_Huge thanks to <@U0ALSG3VA30> and <@U080G9FHV50> for building this_ :purple_heart:

entries.name: hey team! :eyes:
entries.message:
hey team! :eyes:

couple of flow builder updates:
• *we removed "Beta" tag* :chefs-kiss:
    ◦ something that we think now reflects the current state of the product
        ▪︎ *we passed almost 1 million dollars (778k to be clear)* through the flow builder screens and plan to pass even more. also couple of success cases are coming soon.
        ▪︎ we do have 91 company with transactions, with almost 400 flows live :rocket:
    ◦ for transparency - we definitely still have some problems and bugs, but the good thing is that we identified most them and we are now improving the product week by week (a message above as an example). 
        ▪︎ we basically built a figma-like product in a short period of time and for sure there are million of cases to test&fix. team focuses on that and I am happy with their approach
• *we've released the cross-placement AB tests for Flow builder!* :clap:
    ◦ something that is available in old builder for a long time, and we now added it for flow builder as well. I do know couple of names who wanted it badly 
    ◦ to get to the parity with the legacy builder - "custom tags" and "different images by light/dark theme" are coming soon too 
• *we've added the "sliding sheet" element as well*
    ◦ it has the same concept as "overlay" in the legacy builder. background doesn't move, the content does (a short video attached)
    ◦ it's needed for a better migration from the old builder, as well as unlocking different variations for screens building

Release: September 16, 2026
Dependencies: None
Effected areas: Events, Integrations, Webhooks, Event Feed

<!subteam^S03KM96DV0U> <!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ> <@U090BDLA9JN> <@U0ASX4X3CKZ>

entries.name: hey team!
entries.message:
hey team!
couple of Flow Builder updates. today events are connected with analytics :bar_chart:, so customers get not only screens, but data to use it for their growth :rocket:

UPD: NO SDK UPDATE NEEDED!!!

• *app owners can finally receive the user inputs (reading/superunlimited/mobiversite and many others requested that)*
    ◦ now our SDK sends you the info about any input on the users' side within the flow - quiz answer, "name" input or even date/time picked on the date of birth
    ◦ <https://adapty.io/docs/ios-flow-input|learn more here>
• *app owners now receive the screen views data as well*
    ◦ it means that now it's possible to create a funnel analytics on clients' side. we don't offer it in the dashboard yet, but for those who want - they can catch these events and store them on their own to build the funnel analytics etc. something that many clients also requested (sweatcoin for example) 
    ◦ <https://adapty.io/docs/ios-flow-screen-views|learn more here >
• *we added grouping by flow in revenue dashboards (see screenshot). something that clients with live flows asked about*
    ◦ now growth persons can really define which flow brought the revenue and distinguish this data to make conclusions. 
    ◦ <https://adapty.io/docs/flow-metrics#filter-analytics-by-flow|learn more>
huge thanks for PS team too, for highlighting some ideas. and <@U0BB5T65SF6> <@U033TEH5HSA> and QA team for making these tasks possible

entries.name: Hey team, we’ve just launched a new feature for Adapty Attribution: Predicted LTV for Meta Ads.
entries.message:
Hey team, we’ve just launched a new feature for Adapty Attribution: Predicted LTV for Meta Ads.

Instead of sending Meta only the revenue a user generated today, Adapty can send the revenue that user is expected to generate over time.

For example, Meta might normally see:

Trial started: $0
First payment: $9.99

With Predicted LTV, Adapty can tell Meta: This user is expected to generate $45 over 90 days

This matters because Meta’s value optimization is only as good as the conversion values we give it. If we send only the first payment, Meta may optimize toward users who convert cheaply today, not necessarily the users who generate the most revenue over time.

Predicted LTV helps Meta optimize toward long-term subscriber value, not just the first transaction.

It also works naturally with Qualified Trials: Qualified Trials decides which users are worth sending. Predicted LTV tells Meta how much those users may be worth.

Adapty already has the subscription and retention data. Now customers can use that data directly for campaign optimization without building the entire prediction pipeline themselves.

Adapty Attribution is not only about measuring where users came from. We can also improve the quality and value of the signals ad networks use to optimize campaigns.

Together, Attribution + Qualified Trials + Predicted LTV gives us a much stronger signal engineering story for subscription apps.

entries.message:
hey team. last week we tinkered a lot and made a thing — a way to use the *flow builder for coding agents*.

now agents like claude code, cowork and codex can create and edit flows in adapty. and by edit i mean, you know, REAL edit — components, themes, locales, interactivity and everything else that's possible with our builder.

how it it's different from builder ai chat, and why it's important:
• *model ability* — chat: we own model selection and pay for tokens, so user can't use the smartest yet expensive model. skill: user brings his own model, so output quality is capped only by frontier model capabilities, not by adapty economy
• *freedom* — chat: curated selection of tools, more economical and safe, but restricted (no images, no locales, no working outside a single screen yet). skill: full freedom to the agent, whole flow config, no feature limit, better results, but more tokens burned and way less safe
• *look to the future* — chat: good starting point for normies. skill: canvas for pioneers, and i believe we can take inspiration from our most creative skill power users to improve both builder and ai chat

entries.name: Hey everyone! Here's what's been going on with AdaptyMail and why it's been quiet for so long:
entries.message:
Hey everyone! Here's what's been going on with AdaptyMail and why it's been quiet for so long:
*we stand on the Amazon review*

In July Amazon put our sending account under review. While it's open, billing is frozen and we're not onboarding new clients. If we don't clear it, they cut off sending, and without sending there's no product.
The main complaint was about links. A single email pulled them from four different places: some pointed at the client's domain, some at ours, some straight to the App Store, some at Amazon's own tracking addresses. To a spam filter that looks like an email assembled from parts of unclear origin. On top of that, link reputation is scored separately from sender reputation, so one client with a bad list was dragging down the link domains for everyone else.
We've built everything they asked for, and we're sending our response to the review team *today*.

What we did with links
Every client now gets their own link subdomain, something like <http://go.theirdomain.com|go.theirdomain.com>. During setup the client adds one DNS record pointing at us, plus a second housekeeping record so the security certificate renews automatically and nobody has to touch it every three months. From there, every link in the email, all of them, runs through that subdomain.
Then it splits. Images live in our Cloudflare storage and get served directly, no hop involved: the reader sees the client's address, the image comes from us, nobody notices anything.

Clicks work differently. The request reaches us, we record the event, and we send the person on to wherever they were going. The address bar stays on the client's domain the whole time, and nobody ever gets bounced through a domain of ours.
Click tracking is ours now, not Amazon's. Their built-in tracking rewrote links to their own addresses, and those addresses were exactly the foreign element in the email. We turned it off and replaced it with our own. As a side benefit, click data now sits with us instead of in someone else's system with their format and their delay.

What else we did
Email confirmation is live. When an email address shows up on a user, they get a message with a button. Until they press it, no marketing goes out. We built it so a mail provider's security scanner can't press it for them, which happens more often than you'd think and wrecks both the numbers and the point of the whole thing.

We split two things apart: whether an address is confirmed, and whether the person agreed to marketing. The first applies to all mail, service messages included. The second only to marketing, and the person ticks that box themselves in the app.
Each client now gets stopped on their own. If complaints spike for one client, sending pauses for that client and everyone else keeps running. Before, one dirty list could taint everyone's reputation at once.

Next: we wait for Amazon's answer. Once the review lifts, billing and new client onboarding unfreeze.

*Another big thing: FunnelFox integration is live today!*
FunnelFox runs the funnel that takes a user from the web into the app. Adapty Mail now handles the email at every step of it.
Leads from FunnelFox reach us immediately, with nothing for the client to export and nothing to configure on their side. People are split by where they stalled: dropped the quiz, reached checkout and didn't buy, paid and never installed. All three used to get the same email. Now each gets their own.
For clients already on FunnelFox, it's running.

Yo!
Can we have more details and use cases for this FF integration, please?

Sure. Short version: FunnelFox pushes profiles, purchases and subscription changes into one Adapty Mail project, one way, arriving within about a minute of the funnel event. From there Adapty Mail runs the campaigns.
What comes across with each profile: email, customer user ID, country, device, OS, locale, timezone, funnel ID, profile ID, session ID, experiment ID where there is one, and the email consent answer.

Four triggers you can build flows on today:
1. Never purchased. Someone gave you an email in the funnel and didn't buy. Covers both the abandoned quiz and the paywall they walked away from. Use case: objection-handling sequence at +1h, +24h, +72h etc.
2. Renewal cancelled. Auto-renewal is off but access is still live. Use case: a save flow while the window is open.

4. Expired. Subscription lapsed. Use case: winback

There is no backfill, so forwarding starts the moment client save the secret key and nothing from before that point can be re-synced.
Locale/country and experiment ID are the two fields which client could use for personalisation. Country lets you build a segment and send that segment in its native language instead of defaulting everyone to English. Experiment ID identifies the specific funnel someone came through, and a specific funnel is a specific audience. Pull it into its own segment, describe that audience in the campaign prompt, and the generated emails speak to the people who saw that funnel rather than to an average of everyone.

:rocket: *Launching today: Search Popularity + Keyword Suggester*

We are bringing the keyword discovery stage into Adapty.
*Search Popularity* shows ranked App Store search terms for a selected market, genre, and completed period. *Keyword Suggester* expands a seed into related phrase candidates and Apple category context, then helps users build a shortlist.

Important: popularity is a relative research signal, not search volume, conversion, or a performance forecast.

entries.name: Hey team, we’ve been working on a new feature for Adapty Attribution, and it’s now live: Qualified Trials.
entries.message:
Hey team, we’ve been working on a new feature for Adapty Attribution, and it’s now live: Qualified Trials.

With Qualified Trials, customers can choose to send trial events to Meta and TikTok only after a user has stayed in the trial for a defined number of hours without cancelling.

So instead of sending every trial start as a signal, Adapty can send only the higher-quality trial events. This helps customers improve signal quality, reduce noise, and give ad networks better data for campaign optimization.

We can use it to talk about:
• Better signal engineering for subscription apps
• Higher-quality optimization events for Meta campaigns
• Reducing noisy trial signals
• Helping UA teams optimize for users with stronger purchase intent
It’s live on the dashboard. cc <!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ>

Big thanks to <@U08PXEX7CAK> for implementing this so quickly

<!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ> <!subteam^S03KM96DV0U> <!subteam^S03KC9S1QMC> <@U05QELDHUUX> <@U06K36L6CTB>

Sup, team — it’s finally here (under feature flag BUT goes live this week)! :apple:

When a subscriber taps Cancel Subscription in iOS Settings, Apple now shows _your_ message right in the cancellation sheet — a value reminder, a discount, or a plan switch — before the cancellation is confirmed. The one screen apps never owned, now addressable straight from Adapty:

• on-device preview — see the message in Apple’s cancel sheet (light & dark) before it goes to review (Our benefit, only SW support)
• AI localization — write once in English, auto translate fills every locale. (Our benefit, RC and SW doesn’t support this)
• save-rate analytics — Shown / Saved / Save rate per message
Apple’s side is still in beta, so we’re shipping behind a feature flag purely as a safety net. Until it comes off, enable it in the browser console:
`window.adapty_ff.set('retentionMessaging', true)` → Apple Retention Messaging appears in the left nav. Poke around and drop anything odd in this thread. <!subteam^S07BZPQDBUJ> You can provide it to your clients who are approved from Apple, most probably we’ll disable it this week and go LIVE!

*Who this is for:* 
Any iOS subscription app that wants to lift retention with zero engineering - no endpoint, no SDK update. Sharpest fits: price-sensitive apps (discount at cancel intent), monthly + annual mixes (plan switch instead of churn).

*What’s next:* 
Analytics improvements (adding saved $ metric), then A/B testing if adoption is strong.

Docs: <https://adapty.io/docs/retention-messaging|adapty.io/docs/retention-messaging>

*AI Agent (Apple Ads) - what two months of client conversations tell us*

I've analyzed every client conversation with the agent since release. In this post, I'll share the main highlights. You can find the full analysis in the document: <https://app.notion.com/p/adapty/AI-18-27-2026-3aa1ca4355c38197960ee8bc1ee93a55|:bar_chart: AI Agent Chat Analytics> + interactive visualization attached.

*The numbers*:
• 81 client orgs tried the agent → 221 real chats
• *72% of orgs (58) started one chat and never came back* :epic-sad:
• 11 deep sessions with 10+ messages - clients execute its instructions step by step and come back for verification.
*What separates those who stayed from those who left:*
• Churned clients opened with broad questions - "what's wrong with my ads?" in various forms. The agent answered, couldn't create or change anything itself, and the client never returned.
• Retained clients came with specific tasks - "what's up with my ROAS?" - which gives them a reason to come back and re-check regularly. One client literally runs the same weekly-report prompt every Monday across 3–4 apps, polishing it a bit each iteration.
*Potential agent improvements:*
1. Scheduled reports/checks - "check my ROAS every Monday."
2. Agent-initiated follow-ups - client asks "what can I improve?", agent gives recommendations and offers: "Want me to re-check in 3 days and ping you?" with an "Ok, remind me" button. Should lift retention for clients who come with broad questions.
Attached to the message is a visualization of the analytics in the form of an HTML file.
You can also find an MD file with analytics <https://app.notion.com/p/adapty/AI-Agent-Chat-Analytics-May-25-July-28-2026-3aa1ca4355c38197960ee8bc1ee93a55|in the Document>.
